abstracts.abstract: This paper introduces a novel information-theoretic framework for modeling signal integrity in heterogeneous integrated systems, addressing a fundamental gap in VLSI design methodology. Unlike conventional approaches that rely on empirical parasitic extraction, we formulate signal propagation as a communication channel problem within 3D integration stacks. The proposed framework establishes theoretical bounds on crosstalk noise and timing degradation by introducing entropy-based metrics that capture the stochastic nature of switching activity in mixed-signal environments. We derive closed-form expressions for the minimum wire spacing required to achieve target bit-error rates across different technology nodes. The mathematical formulation enables early-stage design space exploration without costly full-wave electromagnetic simulations. Our analysis reveals that traditional worst-case design margins are overly conservative by up to 40% when signal correlation effects are properly accounted for. The framework seamlessly integrates with existing physical design flows, providing designers with theoretical guidance for timing closure in complex SoC implementations. Experimental validation on industrial benchmarks demonstrates that the derived bounds accurately predict signal integrity violations with less than 8% error compared to HSPICE simulations while reducing analysis time by three orders of magnitude. This work establishes a new paradigm for VLSI integration optimization based on information theory principles.

This paper presents a rigorous mathematical analysis that significantly improves timing analysis accuracy for integrated circuits with process variations. Prior work in statistical timing analysis relies on first-order canonical forms that fail to capture non-Gaussian effects in deep sub-micron technologies. We develop a higher-order cumulantexpansion approach that accurately models the distribution of circuit delays under correlated parameter variations. The theoretical contribution includes novel closed-form expressions for the propagation of skewness and kurtosis through logical gates, enabling efficient computation of circuit delay distributions without Monte Carlo sampling. We prove that the proposed method achieves convergence to the true distribution within 2% accuracy for correlation coefficients up to 0.9. The analysis extends naturally to handle spatial correlation in physical design through a covariance decomposition technique. Compared to state-of-the-art SSTA methods, our approach reduces computational complexity from O(n²) to O(n) while improving accuracy on ISCAS85 benchmarks. The mathematical framework is validated against silicon measurement data from a 28nm test chip, demonstrating less than 1% error in predicting the 99.9th percentile delay. This work provides design automation tools with a theoretically sound foundation for timing closure in low-power design applications.

This paper presents ChipletX, a novel chiplet-based system architecture that fundamentally redefines heterogeneous integration for next-generation SoC design. Unlike current approaches that treat chiplets as discrete components connected through silicon interposers, ChipletX introduces a modular communication fabric with configurable protocol bridges enabling seamless integration of diverse technology nodes on organic substrates. The architecture employs a distributed intelligence model where each chiplet contains localized power management and thermal monitoring units coordinated through a central orchestration engine. We demonstrate a 12-chiplet system implemented in 7nm, 12nm, and 28nm nodes achieving 85% bandwidth efficiency improvement over conventional approaches while reducing substrate complexity. The communication architecture supports dynamic bandwidth allocation based on application requirements, enabling runtime optimization between compute, memory, and I/O chiplets. Physical implementation results show a 40% reduction in inter-chiplet wire length compared to monolithic designs with equivalent functionality. The system includes novel debug infrastructure enabling die-level observability during system bring-up. Power domain management achieves 25% reduction in leakage through fine-grained power gating at chiplet boundaries. ChipletX demonstrates that heterogeneous integration through modular chiplets can surpass monolithic SoC performance while enabling yield improvements through die-level redundancy.

This paper presents an improved analog-to-digital converter integration methodology for mixed-signal SoC implementation, addressing the critical challenge of noise coupling in highly integrated systems. The proposed design flow incorporates electromagnetic interference-aware floorplanning with novel guard ring structures that reduce digital switching noise injection into sensitive analog blocks by 18dB compared to conventional techniques. We demonstrate a 12-bit 200MS/s SAR ADC achieving 74dB SNDR in a 28nm CMOS process integrated alongside a 2GHz ARM processor core. The physical design methodology employs a hierarchical approach that separates sensitive analog routing from noisy digital interconnects through dedicated shielding layers. Power delivery network optimization includes on-chip LDOs with dynamic voltage scaling controlled by an integrated digital assist engine. Measurement results show that the ADC maintains performance across processor activity levels without calibration, with INL and DNL below 0.5LSB under all test conditions. The verification methodology includes RTL-to-silicon correlation for noise coupling analysis, reducing validation time by 60%. The design achieves 0.8mW power consumption at peak sampling rate, representing 35% improvement over prior art in similar technology nodes. This work provides a scalable approach for integrating precision analog circuits in digital-dominated SoC platforms.
